reasons.quote: Contributed to a React design system used by the whole team
reasons.problem: Five years at one company in React and TypeScript, with design system work, performance work and mentoring, is the core mid-level frontend profile. That is stronger than most of the pile, which is mainly React and TypeScript with no shared-component or performance evidence. If the numbers get filled in, this is worth 30 minutes.
reasons.fix: Say what the candidate owned in the design system (for example a component set, tokens, accessibility or docs), and give the size and adoption: components, developers and projects. Put the strongest measured result first in the Profile.

reasons.quote: Improved the performance of the main web app by
reasons.problem: The verbs 'Contributed' and 'Improved' show participation, not ownership, and one performance metric is the only outcome on the CV. The recent hands-on level is hard to judge, so interview confidence stays low. Delivery and mentoring bullets will also read as generic unless they carry numbers.
reasons.fix: Rewrite each bullet as 'I did X, which produced Y': what you changed (code-splitting, image optimisation), the before and after metric, and your own role versus the team's. Give real numbers for projects delivered and juniors mentored.

reasons.problem: A frontend manager screens for testing, accessibility, Git and CI/CD. None of them appears anywhere in the CV, so I can't tell whether this person tests or ships with discipline. The earlier roles (WordPress, SEO, a small Vue app) also pull focus away from the React and TypeScript story.
reasons.fix: List only what is really used (Git, Jest or Testing Library, Cypress or Playwright, WCAG, responsive design, CI/CD, Next.js). Tie testing and accessibility to the design system or performance bullets, and cut the freelance WordPress and SEO lines to one short line.
